first_impression: A canal-pavilion departure attendant, brass route boat, large visible drum and gears, and separate real passenger boat make a readable travel-clockwork scene. The face and bob follow the portrait.

gates.evidence: Cord windings and descending weight appear together; the weight bottom/free clearance is cropped and cannot be fully checked.
Large wheel and smaller pinion sit apart on one long horizontal shaft; their teeth do not mesh into the requested transmission chain.
Boat marker and rack are visible above the open frame, but no continuous pinion engagement connects the lower drive to the rack.
Wheel, levers and pendulum are shown; a complete touching-pallet route through a lever to the pendulum cannot be followed.
Same subject holds the separate key in the lowered right hand and rests the opposite hand on the outer frame; both arms are continuous.
Foreground route table and small marker remain distinct from the passenger boat visible through the pavilion opening.
Visible face proportions, lips, short dark bob and fine fringe follow the reference; no identity claim.
